summary: Suspected client-side retry duplication causing sudden embeddings spike and invoice overage
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports an unanticipated 42x spike in embeddings usage for a single job run on 2026-03-11 which produced an unusually large invoice line item. Customer suspects they were not sending that many vectors and requests an audit and provisional credit.

Impact: Large unexpected invoice for $4,180 (line item for embeddings tokens) for a mid-sized batch job. Customer's production app throttled after hitting account limits; this is impacting their analytics pipelines.

Environment: prod cluster in us-east, model open-embed-768-v2, calls from client SDK v2.1.0. Customer indicated most requests come from a batch worker running hourly.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Run batch_predict.sh pointing at dataset batch_analytics_03011.csv (internal customer dataset name)
2) Observe a normal run historically ~10k vectors; on 2026-03-11 observed ~420k vectors consumed
3) No config change reported; client-side code has a retry wrapper around the embeddings call with exponential backoff

Logs / Evidence provided by customer:
- SDK call trace (timestamps redacted) showing repeated identical payloads within 1s windows: request_id a1b2c3 repeated 6x before returning success
- Billing snapshot (CSV) with per-minute counters showing a burst at 2026-03-11T03:12Z
- Job orchestration logs showing the worker process retry loop woke and re-issued payloads when it did not immediately see a success response from the SDK

Customer request: Audit the server-side metering to confirm whether these duplicates were counted as separate embeddings. If duplicates are counted, request provisional credit for the duplicated portion and guidance on preventing billing surprises. Customer also requests an audit window extension to allow them to collect additional logs (they'll share full worker traces).

Additional context: Customer has no dedicated capacity contract and is on pay-as-you-go. They are time-sensitive about credit because they are at risk of disabling ingestion for key pipelines.

investigation_notes: Metering pipeline accepts each inbound HTTP request and emits a meter event; deduplication only occurs if identical idempotency keys are supplied. Customer SDK did not set idempotency key per call; retry wrapper re-sent entire payload generating new request ids.
Correlation query (billing_db): SELECT count(*) FROM meter_events WHERE account = 'kitescale' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-03-11T03:10Z' AND '2026-03-11T03:18Z' => 418,520

Metering raw logs show repeated payload hashes with identical embeddings inputs but different request_ids (uuid v4). SDK v2.1.0's retry helper (exp-backoff) will re-initialize request metadata per attempt - confirmed in uploaded client trace.

Hypothesis: Network flakiness caused initial attempts to time out at app layer; retry wrapper re-sent payloads without idempotency key causing full duplication in billing. Not a server bug in counting, but a lack of client-side idempotency leading to repeated billable events.

Requested Eng to consider short-term mitigation: honor Idempotency-Key header if present; also consider offering a server-side optional lightweight request hashing dedup for embeddings within X seconds as a future feature (linked to feature RFC).
resolution: Provisional credit: Applied a provisional credit of $3,600 on 2026-03-14 while a full audit completes. Action items for customer: upgrade to SDK v2.2.1 (includes idempotency helper) and set per-call Idempotency-Key when wrapping retries; recommended retry strategy documented. Action items for Redwood: Billing to complete final audit by 2026-03-18 and issue final adjustment if duplicates confirmed; Engineering to evaluate a short-term metering dedup approach and create follow-up INT ticket (INT-1032) for product discussion. Awaiting customer confirmation of SDK upgrade before closing.
